native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the PCA of forms of capital analysed in 100-year time slices, the PC1 value at the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is markedly higher (approximately +1.66, with PC1 explaining ~76% of variance) than the six subsequent slices from 1000 to 500 BCE, which cluster between about −0.74 and +0.34 (mean ≈ −0.28); the 1100 BCE level sits roughly 1.9 standardised units (~4 SD) above the rest of the period, driven by high Z-values for depot hoards, copper/gold, house size and monument count at 1100 BCE, after which these capital indicators collapse and PC1 declines to its lowest values around 600–500 BCE.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv (decimal-comma format), dropped group/color, used all 12 pre-Z-scored capital variables as-is. Rows already sit at 100-year slices; the 7 rows 1100–500 BCE form the YBA window. Fitted PCA (SVD) on the pooled 7-slice YBA window, extracted per-slice PC1 scores, and compared the 1100 BCE score against the 1000–500 BCE band. Robustness: (1) PCA refit on the full 39-row record — 1100 BCE remains the positive outlier; (2) refit with zero-variance columns ZSichel/ZKeform dropped — scores identical.
